# tritonctl nat-gateway

Manage NAT gateways

Subcommands: list, show, create, delete

Usage: `tritonctl nat-gateway [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

## tritonctl nat-gateway list

List NAT gateways in the project, or on one VPC

Alias: ls

Usage: `tritonctl nat-gateway list [OPTIONS]`

- `--vpc <VPC>`: Only the gateways of this VPC (name, uuid, or prefix)

## tritonctl nat-gateway show

Show one NAT gateway

Usage: `tritonctl nat-gateway show [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Gateway name, uuid, or prefix

## tritonctl nat-gateway create

Create a NAT gateway on a VPC

Usage: `tritonctl nat-gateway create [OPTIONS] --vpc <VPC> --name <NAME>`

- `--vpc <VPC>`: VPC to serve (name, uuid, or prefix) (required)
- `--name <NAME>` (required)
- `--description <DESCRIPTION>`
- `--family <FAMILY>`: Address family of the public side (one of: v4, v6; default: v4)

## tritonctl nat-gateway delete

Delete a NAT gateway

Alias: rm

Usage: `tritonctl nat-gateway delete [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Gateway name, uuid, or prefix
- `-n, --dry-run`: Print what would change and stop
- `-y, --yes`: Answer yes to the confirmation. The summary still prints
- `--keep-going`: Keep executing after a step fails
